title: Physics — comprehensive review for the grades below 10 (Grade 7–9 program)
note: A grade-by-grade physics test covering the program of the grades below 10. Each question is one atomic idea. Some questions include a diagram and a 'Practice problems' block (with answers) you can pose to him. Grade-10/IGCSE content (lenses, refractive index, induction, half-life, redshift, specific heat, etc.) is deliberately left out.

topics.name: Maths & practical skills (underpin all of physics)

questions.text: Rearrange a simple formula: from speed = distance / time, make distance the subject.

problems.q: Make t the subject of speed = distance / time.

questions.text: Substitute numbers into a formula and give the answer with the correct unit.
Read a measurement accurately from a ruler, a measuring cylinder and a thermometer.
Read a line graph: what does the gradient (steepness) tell you, and what does a flat line mean?
Write a large and a small number in powers of ten (e.g. 3000 and 0.005).

problems.q: Write 0.005 in powers of ten.
Write 3000 in powers of ten.

questions.text: Calculate the area of a rectangle and the volume of a box, with units.

problems.q: A box is 2 m × 3 m × 4 m. Find its volume.

questions.text: Use a fraction, a decimal and a percentage in a simple calculation.

problems.q: Find 20% of 60.

questions.text: Name the basic physical quantities and their units: length, mass, time, temperature.
Name common measuring instruments and what each measures (ruler, balance, stopwatch, thermometer, measuring cylinder).
What is a force? Give an example of a push and of a pull.
Name several different types of force (gravity, friction, magnetic, contact).
How is a force measured — in what unit and with what instrument?
Describe gravity as a force of attraction between masses.
Explain the difference between mass and weight.
Name several forms/stores of energy and describe one energy transfer.
State that energy is conserved, and that it tends to dissipate (spread out, become less useful).
What is density (mass per unit volume)?

problems.q: A block has mass 600 g and volume 200 cm³. Find its density.

questions.text: Describe how you would measure the density of a small stone.
Use the idea of density to explain why some objects float and others sink.
How is sound produced, and why can it not travel through a vacuum?
What causes an echo?
What changes the pitch, and what changes the loudness, of a sound?
Describe electric current as a flow of charge/electrons.
Explain the difference between a conductor and an insulator, with an example of each.
Build a simple series circuit and draw the symbols for a cell, switch, lamp and ammeter.
Where is an ammeter connected, and what happens to the current when you add more lamps in series?
Calculate speed using speed = distance / time.

problems.q: A car travels 150 m in 10 s. Find its speed.
A runner moves at 5 m/s for 12 s. How far does she go?

questions.text: What is meant by average speed?
Interpret a distance–time graph (steady speed, faster, stationary).

problems.q: On a distance–time graph a line is horizontal for 5 s. What is the object doing?

questions.text: Explain the difference between speed and velocity.
What does acceleration mean?
Describe the effect of balanced and unbalanced forces on motion.
Describe friction, and give an example where it is useful and where it is a nuisance.
Find the turning effect of a force using moment = force × distance.

problems.q: A force of 20 N acts 0.5 m from a pivot. Find the moment.
A child of weight 300 N sits 1.0 m from the pivot of a seesaw. How far from the pivot must a 200 N child sit to balance it?

questions.text: Define pressure (force / area); explain why skis or wide tyres reduce pressure on the ground.

problems.q: A box pushes down with 200 N over an area of 0.5 m². Find the pressure.

questions.text: Use the particle model to explain pressure in liquids and gases, and how it changes with depth.
What is atmospheric pressure, and give one piece of evidence that it exists.
Explain the difference between heat and temperature.
Describe how a (liquid-in-glass) thermometer works.
Describe thermal expansion of solids, liquids and gases, with an everyday example.
Describe conduction and give an example.
Describe convection and give an example.
Describe radiation (infrared) and give an example.
State that light travels in straight lines, and explain how we are able to see objects.
State and use the law of reflection.

problems.q: A ray hits a mirror at 30° to the normal. What is the angle of reflection?

questions.text: Describe the image formed in a plane mirror (upright, same size, laterally inverted, virtual).
Describe refraction — light bending when it passes into glass or water — and why it happens.
What does a prism do to white light?
Why does a coloured object (e.g. a red apple) look that colour?
Describe a magnet and its magnetic field, and say which materials are magnetic.
How do you make an electromagnet, how can you make it stronger, and give a use.
Define velocity, and explain how it differs from speed.
Define acceleration and state its unit.
Interpret a speed–time graph: what do the gradient and the area underneath represent?

problems.q: On a speed–time graph the line rises from 0 to 20 m/s in 4 s. Find the acceleration.
A car moves at a steady 15 m/s for 6 s. Use the area under the graph to find the distance.

questions.text: State Newton's first law (inertia) with an example.
Use Newton's second law, F = m × a, in a calculation.

problems.q: A 2 kg trolley accelerates at 3 m/s². Find the resultant force.
A 1500 N force acts on a 500 kg car. Find its acceleration.

questions.text: State Newton's third law with an example.
Define momentum (p = m × v) and calculate it.

problems.q: Find the momentum of a 4 kg ball moving at 5 m/s.

questions.text: State the idea of conservation of momentum (e.g. in a collision).
Describe gravitation as a universal attraction between masses.
What is free fall, and what is the approximate value of g near the Earth's surface?
Calculate work done (work = force × distance) and state its unit.

problems.q: A force of 10 N moves a box 3 m. Find the work done.

questions.text: Calculate kinetic energy (½ × m × v²).

problems.q: Find the kinetic energy of a 2 kg ball moving at 3 m/s.

questions.text: Calculate the change in gravitational potential energy (m × g × h).

problems.q: A 5 kg mass is lifted 2 m (g = 10 N/kg). Find the gain in GPE.

questions.text: Define power (work / time) and calculate it.

problems.q: 300 J of work is done in 6 s. Find the power.

questions.text: What is efficiency, and how is it calculated?
Explain upthrust (buoyancy), and relate floating to density and upthrust.
Define electric current and state its unit.
Define potential difference (voltage) and state its unit; how is a voltmeter connected?
Define resistance and state its unit.
State and use Ohm's law (V = I × R).

problems.q: A component has 6 V across it and 2 A through it. Find its resistance.
A 12 V supply drives current through a 4 Ω resistor. Find the current.

questions.text: Compare how current and voltage behave in series versus parallel circuits.
Calculate electrical power (P = V × I).

problems.q: A lamp runs at 12 V and 2 A. Find its power.

questions.text: Describe that an electric current produces a magnetic effect (electromagnetism), and give a use.
Define the amplitude, wavelength, frequency and period of a wave.
Explain the difference between transverse and longitudinal waves, with an example of each.
Use the wave equation: wave speed = frequency × wavelength.

problems.q: A wave has frequency 50 Hz and wavelength 4 m. Find its speed.

questions.text: Describe the properties of sound waves (reflection/echo, pitch ↔ frequency, loudness ↔ amplitude).
Describe the structure of the atom (a nucleus of protons and neutrons, with electrons around it).
What do atomic (proton) number and mass (nucleon) number mean?
